reports.title: Enbridge Reports Strong Third Quarter Results, Places Over $3 Billion of Gas Transmission Projects Into Service, and Reaffirms 2026 Financial Guidance

guidance.heading: FINANCIAL OUTLOOK
section: The Company reaffirms its 2026 financial guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $20.2 billion and $20.8 billion and DCF per share between $5.70 and $6.10.
The Company also reaffirms its medium-term outlook for adjusted EBITDA, DCF per share, and EPS average compound annual growth rate of approximately 5%.

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS up to C$0.49 from C$0.46 on gas pipeline and utility growth; 2026 guidance reaffirmed
results: Adjusted earnings rose 8% to C$1.1bn, or C$0.49 a share; GAAP EPS jumped to C$0.59, helped by gains on hedging contracts.
Adjusted EBITDA grew to C$4.4bn: gas pipelines (new rate deals) and gas utilities (higher rates) were up, while oil pipelines slipped on lower Mainline volumes and tolls.
Cash flow from operations was C$2.7bn, down from C$2.9bn; distributable cash flow rose to C$2.7bn.
Agreed to buy Tallgrass's crude oil business (US$2.6bn) and closed the Salt Creek Permian gathering deal (US$0.6bn); raised C$3.0bn in new shares to help pay.
Over C$3bn of gas projects entered service; the secured project backlog is about C$38bn. Debt was 5.1x EBITDA, slightly above target, mainly due to the exchange rate.

guidance.summary: Enbridge kept its 2026 targets for adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow per share, and its roughly 5% a year medium-term growth outlook.

items.metric: Adjusted EBITDA, DCF/share and EPS growth

watch: Regulatory approval and closing of the Tallgrass crude oil acquisition.
Mainline volumes and Gulf Coast contract use, which held back the oil pipeline business.
Leadership handover: CEO Greg Ebel retires in January, with Michele Harradence taking over.
